source: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 19 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 19
knowledgePattern: Count attainable integer step totals through a required checkpoint
solution:
The strict inequality and integer terms say that each downward step has size 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8. From 10 to −10 the total drop is 20; from −10 to −50 it is 40.

If the first segment uses a steps, then 3a ≤ 20 ≤ 8a, giving a = 3,4,5,6. Each is attainable: start with a steps of size 3 and distribute the remaining 20 − 3a units among them, adding at most 5 to each.

Similarly the second segment can use any b from 5 to 13. Its 40 − 3b extra units can be distributed in the same way. The possible totals a + b form every integer from 8 to 19.

There are a + b downward transitions from the first term to term k, so k = a + b + 1 ranges from 9 to 20 inclusive: twelve possibilities. Both segment lengths are positive, so the checkpoint index is strictly between 1 and k. The sequence can be continued forever with steps of size 3. Answer D.

hints.body: For a chosen number of steps, find the smallest and largest total drop. Apply those bounds separately to the drop from 10 to −10 and from −10 to −50.

hints.title: Check every count between your bounds
hints.body: Start all the steps at their smallest allowed drop. Add extra units to individual steps without exceeding the largest drop, until you reach the required total.
